equity_bridge.note: Excluded from flows; held at zero because statutory capital is not distributable and reserve risk is asymmetric. Conservative by roughly its GAAP equity.

historical_growth.basis: Restated continuing-operations series FY2022-FY2025 only (post GEHC and GEV spinoffs as reported in the FY2024/FY2025 10-K comparatives). 5-year CAGRs would span the FY2020 conglomerate ($75.8B revenue incl. Vernova and GE Capital) and are null by design.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (high-teens adjusted revenue growth, raised at Q2 2026; H1 2026 GAAP revenue +22.8%), corroborated by the 16.3% restated 3-year revenue CAGR. Equity/book-value CAGR is not usable: shareholders' equity fell from $34.9B (FY2022) to $17.6B (Q2 2026) because the GEV distribution and buybacks removed capital, not because value was destroyed.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and EPS CAGRs are NOT reported: FY2022 EPS was -$0.06 and FY2023 EPS $8.44 includes the GEHC spin gain in discontinued operations, so any EPS CAGR is noise; equity shrank by the Vernova distribution. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (10.7%) trails revenue (16.3%) because FY2022 continuing FCF still carried Vernova-era working-capital releases and because SBC rose from $143M to $325M; the gap is a mix effect, not a conversion problem -- FY2025 owner FCF/adjusted revenue is 16.4%.
historical_growth.notes: CAGR inputs: revenue 29,139 -> 45,855 (GAAP, restated); owner FCF 5,112 (5,255 - 143 SBC) -> 6,939 (7,264 - 325). Share-count history is only continuous from FY2021 (post 1-for-8 reverse split) and only economically comparable from FY2024 Q2 (post Vernova).

scenario_narratives.base: GE Aerospace delivers FY2026 as guided (adjusted revenue ~+18%, operating profit ~$10.65B, FCF ~$9B), then growth steps down to low-double-digit in FY2027 because forgings, castings and labour -- not demand -- gate how fast LEAP output can rise toward Boeing's 47/month and Airbus's 70+/month. Services (~70% of revenue) keep compounding on a ~50,000-engine commercial and ~30,000-engine military installed base, so mix lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin about 50bp a year from 24.7% to 28% by year 9; LEAP equipment margins improve toward breakeven as the fleet matures (the CFM56 pattern) and the durability-kit cutover in early 2027 gradually removes unplanned shop-visit and warranty cost. Cash tax ramps from 15% to 21% as attributes are used. Defense grows with allied budgets but is the smaller, lower-margin leg. The count is held flat; in practice the $20B buyback is shrinking it, which is unmodelled upside.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply chain unlocks faster than management has signalled: LEAP deliveries track the airframers' rate targets in 2027-28, widebody GEnx/GE9X volume rises with 787/777X, and the durability kit restores CFM56-class time-on-wing so the LEAP aftermarket matures into the highest-margin annuity in aerospace. Revenue compounds 14%/12%/10% in years 2-4 and pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 30% by year 9 (about 26.5% operating), with progress collections on a record backlog adding a small working-capital tailwind. Defense orders (+19% FY2025, +12% Q2 2026) provide a second engine. Next-generation programmes (CFM RISE open fan, adaptive-cycle military) extend the duopoly into the 2030s. Same 9% WACC and 20x cap as base: the upside is in the flows, not a cheaper discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Boeing/Airbus dependency bites: a renewed 737 MAX production disruption or a demand shock (recession, fuel spike, geopolitical closure of a major market) stalls LEAP deliveries and, more importantly, flight hours -- and it is the flight-hour-driven aftermarket that carries GE's margin. Revenue growth collapses to 4%/2%/3% in FY2027-29 after a guided FY2026, while LEAP durability shortfalls in harsh-environment fleets keep unplanned removals, AOG compensation and warranty accruals elevated through a delayed kit cutover, pushing pre-SBC EBITDA margin down to 22% before a slow recovery to 24%. Inventory built for the ramp is stranded (working capital consumes 5% of incremental revenue) and capex stays at 3% to hold capacity. Long-term-care reserve strengthening in the run-off insurance book is the tail risk that would turn the zero-valued bridge item into a cash call. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 16x cap reflect a cyclical rather than a compounder exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: GE Aerospace is valued as a pure-play jet-engine franchise from FY2025 forward; nothing before the 2023/2024 spinoffs is used except the restated continuing-operations revenue and FCF series. The engine is the house owner-FCF component build: adjusted revenue compounds from FY2026 guidance, pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands with services mix, SBC (0.75% of revenue) is expensed and the diluted count held flat, cash tax ramps to statutory, and the run-off insurance book is carried at zero outside the flows. A single 9% USD WACC is used across scenarios; risk is charged in the scenario flows and the 20/50/30 weighting. The market price embeds a lower discount rate and a longer runway than the base case -- the required-return table shows what return today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Boeing/Airbus production-rate dependency: GE cannot ship more LEAPs than the airframers absorb; a MAX disruption throttles both equipment revenue and the later aftermarket ramp

LEAP durability: time-on-wing shortfalls in harsh-environment fleets keep shop-visit, AOG and warranty costs elevated until the HPT-blade kit fully cuts over (early 2027); slippage would hit the margin path directly
Supply chain and labour (forgings, castings, superalloys) cap the delivery ramp -- management's stated binding constraint for 2027
Flight-hour cyclicality: ~70% of revenue is aftermarket, which is resilient but ultimately tracks global utilisation; a recession or fuel shock hits the high-margin leg
Legacy liabilities: run-off long-term-care insurance reserves (carried at zero here) and residual pension obligations can create cash calls unrelated to aerospace
Valuation duration: ~60% of base-case value is terminal; each 1pp on WACC moves value by roughly a fifth, and the market price implies a discount rate well below 9%
Tax: cash tax rate rises from ~15% toward 21% as attributes are consumed; a slower ramp is modest upside, a faster one modest downside
Tariffs, export controls and rare-earth sourcing rules add cost and contract friction across a global supplier base

data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000040545): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-01-29 (revenue, SBC, D&A, intangible amortisation, interest income, income tax provision, share repurchases) and Q2 2026 10-Q filed 2026-07-16 (cash incl. restricted, total borrowings, NCI, shares outstanding, diluted weighted shares); research/GE/Reports/GE_Metrics.csv for the restated FY2022-FY2025 series

inputs.revenue_basis: FY2025 ADJUSTED revenue (GE Aerospace definition, ex run-off insurance premiums and other non-operating revenue) of $42.3B. GAAP total revenues were $45,855M; the ~$3.5B gap is almost entirely insurance revenues of the run-off Employers Reassurance book, which is excluded from the flows (see equity_bridge and notes). FY2026 guidance ('high-teens revenue growth', operating profit $10.55-10.75B, FCF $8.9-9.2B) is framed on the adjusted basis, so the model compounds from it.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 1,037.56M common shares outstanding (10-Q balance sheet, CommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~7M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted 1,047M less basic 1,040M weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $20B authorisation ($4.5B spent H1 2026) funds a falling count in practice, which is upside to the flat convention, not modelled. Post-2021 counts are on the 1-for-8 reverse-split basis; the Q2 2021 CSV row (8,781M) is the only post-2020 row still on the pre-split basis and every pre-FY2020 row is pre-split AND pre-spinoff -- neither is a per-share basis for this business.
inputs.debt_note: Total borrowings $19,157M at 2026-06-30 (DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount = $17,157M long-term + $2,000M current). Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash $9,345M at 2026-06-30. Operating lease liabilities (~$1.06B) are NOT in debt: under ASC 842 the lease cost already sits inside operating profit, so treatment (B) applies with no separate lease charge. NB the Metrics.csv FY2025 TotalDebt of 22,155 is a double count (LongTermDebt tag 20,469 already includes the 1,686 current portion; the combined tag reads 20,494) -- the Q2 2026 CSV value of 19,157 is correct.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income was $144M in FY2025 (InvestmentIncomeInterest) but GE Aerospace is a NET DEBT company (~$9.8B), so the cash pile is not added to EV and its interest is NOT stripped from the flows. Recorded here for auditability only.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $325M (FY2024 $286M). No separate equity-award tax-withholding line is tagged; the combined figure is therefore the expense itself. SBC is 0.77% of adjusted revenue -- immaterial to the house/street band.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $7,551M; H1 2026 $4,527M against the $20B December-2025 authorisation. Dividend raised 30.6% to $0.36/quarter in Feb-2026 (~$1.5B/yr). Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (count held flat, SBC expensed).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (Friday session; valuation dated the following Monday, no after-hours print)
inputs.guidance_vintage: FY2026 guidance as raised at Q2 2026 results (2026-07-16)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 gives cost of equity ~9.7%; ~5% debt weight at ~3.6% after tax pulls WACC to ~9.4%. Rounded DOWN to 9.0% to reflect the ~70% recurring aftermarket mix and duopoly structure; the required-return table and the 7-11% sensitivity grid show how steeply this long-duration valuation moves with the rate. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, Boeing/Airbus rate risk and LEAP durability are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: ASC 842 operating lease expense is already inside operating profit/EBITDA, so no separate lease_cost_pct_path and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; noncontrolling interest ($227M at 2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI share of net income was -$6M in FY2025, so no leakage rate is applied.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials'; adaptations file read for leases, NCI, non-operating assets and risk-charged-once). Fresh build -- no prior GE valuation in this folder. STRUCTURAL: GE HealthCare spun 2023-01-03 and GE Vernova 2024-04-02; every metric before FY2022 in the Metrics.csv describes the old conglomerate (aviation + healthcare + power + GE Capital) and is informational only. The XBRL FY2022-FY2025 series is restated continuing operations (GE Aerospace + run-off insurance) and is the only history used for a CAGR. NON-OPERATING: the run-off insurance business (Employers Reassurance) is excluded from revenue and flows and carried at ZERO in the bridge -- its statutory capital is not extractable and GE's funding obligations were completed in 2024; this is conservative by roughly its GAAP equity, and its risk (long-term-care reserve strengthening) is asymmetric downward, which is why zero rather than book. Legacy pension obligations are not bridged: the principal plans are close to fully funded post-2024 and service cost is inside operating profit; a material deficit would be a bridge deduction. BUYBACKS: flat count is a convention -- GE is an active repurchaser, so the convention is funded. Company FCF ($7.7B FY2025, $8.9-9.2B FY2026 guide) is levered, pre-SBC and ex-insurance; the model's year-1 unlevered owner FCF of ~$8.9B pre-interest and post-SBC is consistent with it.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 18% = FY2026 guidance midpoint of 'high teens' (H1 2026 ran +22.8% GAAP; Q2 +21%). Y2 11% reflects management's own statement that supply chain (forgings, castings, labour), not demand, governs 2027 -- LEAP output rises with Boeing 737 MAX toward 47/month and A320neo toward 70+/month but at a slowing rate, while services keep growing low-double-digit off the ageing CFM56/LEAP base. Decay to 3.5% by Y10 as the LEAP fleet matures and the narrowbody cycle normalises.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margins are PRE-SBC (engine deducts sbc_pct separately). FY2025 actual: adjusted operating profit $9.1B + D&A $1.22B + SBC $0.33B = $10.65B / $42.3B = 25.2%. FY2026 guide: $10.65B OP + ~$1.35B D&A + ~$0.37B SBC on ~$49.9B = 24.7% -- flat-to-down because record LEAP equipment deliveries carry breakeven-to-negative margin. Path then expands ~50bp/yr as (i) services mix rises with the installed base, (ii) LEAP equipment margins move toward breakeven as unit costs fall, as CFM56 did, and (iii) the durability kit (full cutover early 2027) cuts warranty/unplanned shop-visit cost. Terminal 28.0% pre-SBC = ~24.5% operating margin, between today's CES segment (~27%) and DPT (~13%).
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 GAAP provision 14% of pretax ($1,405M/$10,000M); FY2024 cash taxes $852M = 11% of pretax. GE still carries tax attributes and benefits from OBBBA expensing, so the CASH rate starts at 15% and ramps to the 21% statutory rate by Y7 as attributes are consumed. Applied to unlevered EBIT.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2025 capex $1,273M (3.0% of adjusted revenue) with GE investing ~$1B+/yr in US manufacturing and MRO capacity; eases to 2.7% as the ramp completes. D&A $1,220M FY2025 (2.9%) held at 2.7% of a larger base. Working capital neutral: progress collections and deferred revenue (~$10.2B) on record orders offset the inventory build of the LEAP ramp -- H1 2026 FCF ($4.35B) ran at ~net income, consistent with zero net capture.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because two independent high-severity risks -- Boeing/Airbus build-rate execution (a recurring pattern at Boeing) and LEAP durability through the 2027 kit cutover -- are outside GE's control, and the price already discounts a long expansion, so a stumble is punished. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs the supply chain, the durability kit and airframer rates to all come good together, which management itself is not promising for 2027. Base 50% because FY2026 guidance has been raised twice and H1 delivered above it.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
